caption: The drawing depicts a rectangular wooden sign bordered by a frame with weathered blue-green paint and touches of yellow and brown, giving an aged appearance. At the top and bottom of the frame, there are faded gold letters; the top appears to spell out “INN” and another unclear word, possibly “TAVERN” or a place name, while the bottom also says “INN.” The center of the sign features a detailed depiction of a bison’s or bull’s head, rendered in brown, white, and gray tones to highlight the animal’s facial features, fur texture, and prominent horn pointing to the right. The background inside the main panel shows wood grain texture and muted earthy colors. The entire sign is topped and bottomed with curved decorative elements, also painted in the weathered blue-green and yellow colors, and there are metal eyelets and rusty hooks at the top corners indicating it was meant to be hung. The sign is placed against a plain, light background.
title: Tavern Sign
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
